investigations.name: tstmd-contraction-reorientation
investigations.description: REAL output of the TST-MD engine, driven CPU-only via the viva-tstmd Docker bridge (TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3). This study evaluates the paper-faithful coupling bar and FAILS it: across every parameter regime tried (fiber stiffness stiff->soft, crosslink density, contractility lambda up to 400, MD noise md_kT, adhesion-annihilation penalty, gradient vs uniform displacement selection) the cell contracts but its adhesions stay frozen in place — the cell detaches from the ECM rather than dragging it inward. This is the open cell-ECM coupling / calibration gap, reported as a failing reproduction, not hidden.
investigations.title: Cell–ECM mechanical coupling (real TST-MD, 2D) — NOT reproduced
investigations.objective: Does the real 2D static-adhesion hybrid CPM + bead-spring ECM engine (Tsingos et al. 2023, the published ancestor of Merks' 3D model) reproduce the paper's core mechanical-reciprocity result — a contractile cell that drags its focal adhesions and the attached, crosslinked ECM inward, reorienting and densifying the matrix?

investigations.name: tstmd-network-connectivity
investigations.description: REAL output of the TST-MD engine via the viva-tstmd Docker bridge. This study evaluates the paper-faithful percolation bar and FAILS it: at CPU-tractable sizes the giant component rises from 0.0007 (no crosslinks) but SATURATES at ~0.30 even at ~13000 created crosslinks — the network never percolates. The onset of connectivity is reproduced; full percolation (the regime the paper's mechanics depend on) is not.
investigations.title: ECM network percolation vs crosslinking (real TST-MD, 2D) — NOT reproduced
investigations.objective: Does the real 2D bead-spring ECM engine reproduce the paper's network percolation (Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 2B) — the giant component rising to a fully connected (~1.0) network at high crosslinking, the regime in which the matrix mechanically resists and transmits cell forces long-range?
